Compared with traditional stereo technology, spatial audio delivers a broader and more immersive acoustic experience. While traditional stereo can only create sound differences between the left and right channels, spatial audio rendering expands sound into the entire surrounding environment, covering not only the horizontal plane but also sources above and below the listener—bringing it closer to real-world perception. For example, when a user approaches a sound source, the volume increases as the distance decreases, providing auditory feedback consistent with real-life experience.
The core principle of spatial audio lies in simulating the human auditory system. By leveraging the propagation and reflection patterns of sound waves in space, multichannel playback, and head-tracking systems, it models the acoustic characteristics of the human ear based on HRTF (Head-Related Transfer Function) to reconstruct sound in 3D spaces. These technologies enable users to perceive not just the direction of sound, but also its distance, orientation, and other spatial cues—resulting in a realistic, multidimensional, and immersive listening experience.
![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/33c32895caf840009e2217e11591662d~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image)
## Spatial audio types
In practical applications, spatial audio can generally be divided into three categories: channel audio, ambient audio, and object audio. These three types of audio complement each other in different use cases through their respective characteristics. Channel audio provides stable and original sound reproduction, ambient audio enhances directional sense and creates an atmosphere, while object audio provides users with a realistic sense of space and interactive experience. By combining these audio types appropriately, it is possible to implement immersive auditory effects within an app.
### Channel audio
Channel audio maps each channel of the audio signal directly to the output of the playback device, without spatialization or reverb processing. In this mode, sound is independent of the user's spatial position or orientation. For example, no matter how the user turns their head, the sound from the left channel always comes from the left side, and the sound from the right channel always comes from the right side. This approach more closely resembles traditional stereo rendering.
### Ambient audio
Ambient audio can be adjusted based on the relative orientation between the sound source and the listener, but it does not reflect changes in distance. Users can hear sound within the directional range of the sound source, but cannot hear anything outside this range. However, even if the user moves closer to or farther from the sound source, the volume does not change significantly. Ambient audio is typically used in scenarios where there are certain requirements for spatial direction but distance does not need to be emphasized, such as background sounds or ambient effects in virtual environments.
### Object audio
Object audio can fully simulate the properties of sound sources in the real world, including position, direction, and distance. The system automatically detects the spatial coordinates and orientation of the sound source, and adjusts the audio output effect in real time based on the relative relationship between the user and the sound source. This allows users not only to distinguish whether a sound is coming from the front, back, left, or right, but also to clearly perceive how near or far the sound source is. For example, when the sound source gradually approaches, users will perceive an increase in volume and changes in spatial positioning. Object audio is widely used in games, virtual reality, and immersive experiences, and serves as an important foundation for realistic interaction.

1. Create an `Entity` instance.
2. Load an audio file:
   Call the `AudioResource.load(filepath)` function to load the audio file as `audioResource`.
3. Add a spatial audio component:
   1. Create a spatial audio component and set its parameters.
   2. Call `entity.components.set()` to add this spatial audio component to the `Entity` instance.
4. Get the playback controller:
   Call the `entity.prepareAudio( audioResource)` function to obtain the `audioPlayerController` associated with `audioResource`.
5. Control audio playback:
   Use `audioPlayerController.play()`, `audioPlayerController.pause()`, `audioPlayerController. setLoop()`, `audioPlayerController.stop()`, and similar functions to control audio playback. You can also use entity's relevant methods to control audio playback. For specific interfaces and instructions, refer to the [API Reference](https://developer-cn.picoxr.com/spatial-api/index.html).

## Important notes

* Before calling `entity.prepareAudio()` or `entity.playAudio()`, you must first add a spatial audio component to the entity.
* Only one type of audio component can be added to the same entity; you cannot add `ObjectAudioComponent`, `AmbientAudioComponent`, and `ChannelAudioComponent` at the same time.
* Each `AudioResource` corresponds to one `AudioPlayerController` instance.
* Per app, you can create up to 40 `AudioPlayerController` instances for Object Audio and Ambient Audio combined, and up to 40 `AudioPlayerController` instances for Channel Audio. Exceeding these limits will cause creation to fail, so be sure to plan the number of `AudioPlayerController` instances carefully.
   At the system level, a total of up to 256 `AudioPlayerController` instances are supported for Object Audio and Ambient Audio combined, and up to 256 `AudioPlayerController` instances for Channel Audio.

## Use different audio components
You can use different audio components based on actual needs. For detailed instructions, refer to the following articles:

* [Use the ChannelAudioComponent](/en_use-channel-audio-component)
* [Use the AmbientAudioComponent](/en_use-ambient-audio-component)
* [Use the ObjectAudioComponent](/en_use-object-audio-component)

## Manage audio resources
Good management of audio resources is crucial for app performance and user experience. For more information, refer to "[Audio resource](/audio-resource)".
